title: Objective scoreboard · what each side actually achieved
dek: Grade documented objectives against observable outcomes. Later, easier Iranian goals do not erase earlier harder ones: a verified retreat is shown as a downgrade from the original benchmark.

scale.label: FAILED / OPPOSITE
scale.meaning: The objective is not achieved and the observable position is at or moving away from it.

scale.label: WEAK
scale.meaning: Some residual leverage or pieces remain, but the objective itself is mostly unmet.

scale.label: PARTIAL / OPEN
scale.meaning: Material elements are achieved or preserved, but the objective is incomplete or the controlling end state remains unresolved.

scale.label: SUBSTANTIAL
scale.meaning: Most of the objective is supported by evidence, although important limits remain.

scale.label: ACHIEVED / CONTROLLING
scale.meaning: The objective is implemented or independently supported as the controlling current outcome.

US1.title: President Trump’s Clear and Unchanging Objectives Drive Decisive Success Against Iranian Regime
US1.supports: Defines wartime U.S. objectives as destroying or severely degrading Iran's ballistic missiles and production capacity, navy/power projection, proxy support, and denying Iran a nuclear weapon. The compilation quotes Vice President Vance saying the regime's fate is incidental to the primary nuclear-denial objective.
US1.quality: PRIMARY / OFFICIAL-ACTOR; defines stated objectives, not independent proof of success

US2.title: National Security Presidential Memorandum/NSPM-2
US2.supports: Formal U.S. policy: deny Iran a nuclear weapon and ICBMs; neutralize regional aggression; disrupt, degrade or deprive the IRGC and surrogates of resources; counter missile and asymmetric/conventional capabilities; apply maximum economic pressure.

US3.title: President Trump’s Iran Agreement Is America First in Action
US3.supports: The administration presented the June agreement as serving U.S. objectives by preventing an Iranian nuclear weapon and reopening Hormuz to free navigation, rather than by destroying or occupying Iran.
US3.quality: PRIMARY / OFFICIAL-ACTOR; defines objective and agreement framing

US4.title: Operation Economic Outcast: Total Isolation of the Iranian Regime
US4.supports: Defines the current economic phase as severing economic lifelines sustaining the Iranian regime and its threat networks until Tehran is isolated and financially broken.
US4.quality: PRIMARY / OFFICIAL-ACTOR; defines current economic objective

IR1.title: Never again: Why Iran denies concessions and negotiates from position of strength
IR1.supports: Presented missile, nuclear and defense capabilities as non-negotiable and framed Iran as the battlefield victor that would dictate terms rather than concede under pressure.

IR2.title: With strategic upper hand, Iran conditions nuclear talks on war's definitive end – on its terms
IR2.supports: Said the end state must record a decisive, substantive Iranian victory rather than symbolic survival.

IR3.title: The logic of victory: Iran's principled terms for end to imposed war define a new strategic reality
IR3.supports: Called compensation, asset return, U.S. withdrawal, blockade termination, protection of allies, sanctions relief and a signed settlement the minimum acceptable outcome; treated Hormuz sovereignty/tolls as a prize already won.

IR4.title: Lessons of war: Strait of Hormuz control and nuclear sovereignty define Iran's inviolable red lines today
IR4.supports: Described nuclear industry, absolute Hormuz sovereignty, defensive/asymmetric capabilities and the Axis of Resistance as non-negotiable strategic capital.

IR5.title: Iran's VP: Tehran will maintain control of Strait of Hormuz
IR5.supports: Aref said management of Hormuz would remain Iran's responsibility and vessels should contribute to service costs.
IR5.quality: IRANIAN OFFICIAL POSITION VIA STATE MEDIA

IR6.title: Iran's Pezeshkian Calls for End to War with US
IR6.supports: Reported Pezeshkian arguing Iran should end the war while it could still describe itself as acting from power and dignity — a materially narrower end-state formulation than the May victory ledger.

IR7.title: Iran's Oil Exports Drop to Zero, Central Bank Governor Confirms
IR7.supports: Reported Hemmati's televised admission that oil exports had halted and access to foreign reserves remained constrained.

us_objectives.assessment: Iran accepted a no-nuclear-weapon commitment and an IAEA-linked stockpile/downblending mechanism in the June framework, but that instrument collapsed and no final controlling nuclear settlement is yet established. The objective is not failed, but it is not complete.

Iran retains missiles, drones and coercive options, so this cannot be scored as total destruction. But the independent current record describes a much narrower Iranian escalation menu after sustained attacks on launch, naval and strike infrastructure. Residual capability prevents a 4/4; the observable degradation supports a strong partial result.

us_objectives.objective: Reduce Iran's ability to arm and sustain proxies
us_objectives.assessment: Iran's regional network has lost freedom and depth, and the regional response has become more coordinated, but Houthi pressure remains operationally relevant and specific tactical control cannot be assumed. The objective is materially advanced, not completed.

The Oman-Iran temporary joint-corridor framework and U.S. mine-clearance activity move toward this objective, but traffic remains far below normal and a permanent navigation regime is not yet controlling. This is progress, not completion.

us_objectives.objective: Use economic isolation to narrow Tehran's options
us_objectives.assessment: Iranian crude flows and offers have fallen, major counterparties are de-risking, domestic fuel stress is visible, and sanctions have broadened toward third-country facilitators. Iran still has trading partners and has not been economically broken, so the objective remains active rather than complete.

iran_objectives.assessment: No implemented reparations payment is established. The June MOU discussed reconstruction rather than completed reparations, and the successor maritime process does not restore this demand.
The June MOU contained a favorable asset-access promise, but it did not mature into durable broad access before collapse. Iranian reporting still describes constrained access to foreign reserves.
Iran briefly received blockade relief under the June MOU, but that gain was reversed. The blockade and export-denial architecture remain central to current U.S. pressure.
Comprehensive relief did not become controlling. Washington is broadening sanctions and third-country pressure while Tehran negotiates under that pressure.

iran_objectives.objective: U.S. withdrawal from bases surrounding Iran
iran_objectives.assessment: No controlling settlement or observable force posture establishes the broad regional U.S. withdrawal Tehran demanded. The June MOU's narrower post-final-deal withdrawal trigger never matured.

iran_objectives.origin: May 22 minimum acceptable outcome / May 27 red line
iran_objectives.assessment: Aligned actors remain, so the network has not disappeared. But no durable settlement guarantee protecting the Axis is established, and the regional security architecture has moved toward constraining rather than protecting Iran-aligned pressure networks.

iran_objectives.objective: Permanent Iranian Hormuz sovereignty / management / fees
iran_objectives.assessment: Iran retains meaningful coercive and temporary operational leverage. But the Aug. 25 mechanism is joint with Oman, contemplates littoral-state consultation and international law, and does not recognize unilateral permanent Iranian control or a compulsory transit-toll right.

iran_objectives.objective: No concessions on nuclear, missiles, defense or regional architecture
iran_objectives.assessment: The final nuclear and missile bargain remains unresolved, so this cannot be scored as a full failure. But Iran has already accepted mediated sequencing and a shared Hormuz architecture inconsistent with the earlier all-or-nothing claim that the regional/security pillars would not be traded under pressure.

iran_walkbacks.from: Decisive substantive victory recorded in the settlement; concrete minimum terms including reparations, assets, U.S. withdrawal, blockade termination, sanctions relief, Axis protection and Hormuz gains.
Settlement must record decisive victory and satisfy the May minimum ledger.
iran_walkbacks.to: End the war while Iran can still describe itself as retaining 'power and dignity.'
iran_walkbacks.assessment: This is a narrower success criterion. It does not erase the earlier benchmark; Atlas records it as a walk-back from the original objective set.

iran_walkbacks.type: BEHAVIORAL RETREAT · NOT A FORMAL NEW OBJECTIVE
iran_walkbacks.from: Washington must reverse coercion / restore the old bargain first; Iran claimed unilateral or dominant Hormuz authority as a strategic gain.
iran_walkbacks.to: Iran validates Pakistani mediation and accepts a joint Oman maritime framework before the old economic package is restored.
iran_walkbacks.assessment: The changed behavior is observable even if Tehran does not formally announce a new objective. It is therefore shown as retreat from the earlier bargaining position, not silently promoted to an equal replacement objective.

not_documented_as_required_us_victory_co: Regime change as a mandatory condition of military success
Eliminate every remaining Iranian coercive capability

semantic_test.title: Do not change either side's scoreboard after the fact
semantic_test.text: Iran's survival does not prove U.S. failure unless destroying Iran was a documented U.S. objective. Conversely, a later Iranian shift from 'decisive victory on our terms' to 'end the war with power and dignity' cannot be used to erase the earlier, harder Iranian victory conditions. Atlas keeps the original benchmark visible and marks verified retreats as downgrades.

precision_note: The 0–4 scores are ordinal evidence grades, not percentages and not claims of mathematical precision. Official sources define stated objectives; they do not self-certify success. Outcomes are graded against the broader independent Atlas record. No composite winner score is calculated because the objectives are not equally weighted.
